lines.text: Charge on an ion or formula of an ionic compound → groups 1, 2, 13 form $1+$, $2+$, $3+$ and groups 15, 16, 17 form $3-$, $2-$, $1-$; balance the charges in the smallest whole-number ratio, with brackets round a repeated polyatomic ion, as in $\ce{Ca3(PO4)2}$ ({{lesson:2.1}})

Compare lattice enthalpies, or the strength of metallic bonding → higher ion charge and smaller ionic radius (data booklet, section 10) give a stronger electrostatic attraction ({{lesson:2.1}}, {{lesson:2.10}})

Draw a Lewis formula → count valence electrons (one more per negative charge, one fewer per positive), join with single bonds, give outer atoms octets, put leftovers on the central atom, then make a multiple bond if it is still short of eight (not for Be or B) ({{lesson:2.2}})

Shape or bond angle → count electron domains on the central atom, a multiple bond as one: 2 linear $180^\circ$, 3 trigonal planar $120^\circ$, 4 tetrahedral $109.5^\circ$; name the shape from the atoms only, and each lone pair closes the angles by about $2.5^\circ$ ({{lesson:2.3}})
Is the molecule polar? → polar bonds ($\Delta\chi$ from the data booklet, section 9) and a shape in which the bond dipoles do not cancel ({{lesson:2.4}})

Compare boiling points of molecular substances → list the forces: London always, dipole–dipole if polar, hydrogen bonding if H is on N, O or F; at similar molar mass the stronger type wins, and with the same forces more electrons or more surface contact wins ({{lesson:2.6}})

Explain a melting point or conductivity → name the structure first: molecular (intermolecular forces overcome), covalent network (covalent bonds broken), ionic (ions move only when molten or dissolved) or metallic (delocalized electrons) ({{lesson:2.1}}, {{lesson:2.5}}, {{lesson:2.10}})

$R_\text{F}$ asked → distance from the baseline to the centre of the spot divided by distance from the baseline to the solvent front; identify by matching references run under the same conditions ({{lesson:2.7}})
Type of bonding in a binary compound → average $\Sigma\chi$ across and difference $\Delta\chi$ up on the bonding triangle (data booklet, section 17) ({{lesson:2.11}})

Addition polymer → repeating unit: the two $\ce{C=C}$ carbons, now singly bonded, keep their groups, with an open bond at each end; monomer: mark off two chain carbons and put the double bond back ({{lesson:2.12}})

Central atom in period 3 or below with five or six domains → trigonal bipyramidal (lone pairs equatorial) or octahedral; several possible Lewis formulas → formal charge = valence − ½ bonding − non-bonding electrons, and the one closest to zero is preferred ({{lesson:2.8}})
Hybridization or $\sigma$ and $\pi$ count → 4, 3 or 2 domains give sp³, sp² or sp; every bond has one $\sigma$, a double bond adds one $\pi$ and a triple bond two ({{lesson:2.9}})
